note: One collapsed footnote per data table: source, extraction, rows and columns. Rendered by tools/table_notes.py; asserted by tools/figure_census.py --gate.

over6.source: PUMPS on this page, built each run from the mWater water-point register, MadAvance group aaaf0a14… (wp_madavance.csv), the preventive-maintenance form de26d89a… (pm.csv), the repair-after-breakdown form 958b4763… (reparation_apres_panne.csv), the call-centre form c08b3fe2… (appel_signalement_pannes.csv), the water-quality results form 7b33c5d7… (wq_results.json) and the WorldPop allocation run (SDWS 1).
over6.extracted: Pulled from mWater on these dates — the newest record in each can be earlier: register ; maintenance ; repairs ; call centre . Water quality .
over6.filter: The actively managed portfolio only — pumps we maintain and that serve people, broken ones included — filtered to the scope selected at the top of the page. A row is a pump whose maintenance clock is more than six months old at the newest activity date in the extracts: it runs from the last maintenance visit or repair, or, for a pump never visited, from its rehabilitation or construction date (shown as “never” in Last visit). Pumps with no works record of any kind have no clock; they are counted separately, not listed here.
over6.columns: Last visit: the later of the last preventive visit and the last repair. Days: from that visit to the newest activity date in the extracts. Last status: the latest answered status by date across call, visit and repair records, the call winning a same-day tie (tools/build_call_tables.py). People: the pump’s WorldPop allocation after its capacity cap. Last WQ: the date of the latest SDWS 3 result, marked fail when E. coli was above the pass threshold.

itin.source: ROUTES on this page: a catch-up route plan drawn from the overdue list above, with road time between stops. It is stored in the page and no build step redraws it; it is on the recorded ungenerated backlog.
itin.extracted: Stops are pumps from the overdue list; their register attributes come from the register pulled . The plan itself is as drawn.
itin.filter: The actively managed portfolio only — pumps we maintain and that serve people, broken ones included — filtered to the scope selected at the top of the page. Overdue pumps only, one site at a time, in visiting order.
itin.columns: Day: route day, with the day’s road distance and hours. Days since visit: as in the overdue list when the plan was drawn. People: the pump’s people served, as in the overdue list.

downtbl.source: DOWN on this page, written each run by tools/build_call_tables.py from the call-centre form c08b3fe2… (appel_signalement_pannes.csv), the preventive-maintenance form de26d89a… (pm.csv) and the repair-after-breakdown form 958b4763… (reparation_apres_panne.csv), joined to the mWater water-point register, MadAvance group aaaf0a14… (wp_madavance.csv).
downtbl.extracted: Pulled from mWater on these dates — the newest record in each can be earlier: register ; maintenance ; repairs ; call centre .
downtbl.filter: The actively managed portfolio only — pumps we maintain and that serve people, broken ones included — filtered to the scope selected at the top of the page. A row is a pump whose latest answered status is “down”.
downtbl.columns: Reported: the date of the record that set the status. Days down: from that date to the build’s cut-off date. Via: which kind of record set it. People: the pump’s WorldPop allocation after its cap.

parttbl.source: PARTIAL on this page, written each run by tools/build_call_tables.py from the same three activity forms as the down list, joined to the mWater water-point register, MadAvance group aaaf0a14… (wp_madavance.csv).
parttbl.extracted: Pulled from mWater on these dates — the newest record in each can be earlier: register ; maintenance ; repairs ; call centre .
parttbl.filter: The actively managed portfolio only — pumps we maintain and that serve people, broken ones included — filtered to the scope selected at the top of the page. A row is a pump whose latest answered status is “partially working”; the buttons above split service requests from reduced performance.
parttbl.columns: Reported: the date of the record that set the status. Status: service request or reduced performance, from the call’s issue question where it was answered, otherwise carried forward, never invented. Comment: the caller’s own words.

opentbl.source: OPENREP on this page, rebuilt every build by tools/build_call_tables.py from the call-centre and repair extracts: a managed pump reported down to the call centre since 1 March 2026 with no repair record, on either repair source, dated on or after that report.
opentbl.extracted: The call-centre and repair extracts were pulled and ; the rows are rebuilt from them.
opentbl.filter: The actively managed portfolio only — pumps we maintain and that serve people, broken ones included — filtered to the scope selected at the top of the page. A row is an open down-report with no repair record dated on or after it. A repair record dated the same day as the report closes it here, although the status rule lets a call win over a repair on a shared date, so a pump can be down in the list above and not open here (a repair was recorded that day, so it is not waiting for one).
opentbl.columns: Reported down: the earliest such report. Days open: from that report to the build date. Latest status: the pump’s current status, by the same rule as the down list above.

poptbl.source: PUMPS and the WorldPop allocation (SDWS 1) on this page, run on WorldPop R2025A with the barrier clip and capacity caps; the roof-count census from roof-count form 8aa2dd78… (roof_count.json).
poptbl.extracted: Register pulled ; roof counts pulled ; allocation run of .
poptbl.filter: The actively managed portfolio only — pumps we maintain and that serve people, broken ones included — filtered to the scope selected at the top of the page. One row per site, then the total.
poptbl.columns: With a WorldPop figure: pumps the allocation covers. WorldPop (capped): the sum of each pump’s allocation after its capacity cap. Roof-count census: the sum of roofs ÷ the roofs-per-household factor × household size. Difference: WorldPop against the roof count, as a percentage of the roof count.

recontbl.source: REG.recon on this page: the pumps that sat between the dashboard count and the successful-rehabilitation count, assembled by hand from the register and the first-rehabilitation records. No build step recomputes it; it is on the recorded ungenerated backlog.
recontbl.extracted: Assembled from the register and the combined rehabilitation form 86cf66ef…; those extracts were last pulled and .
recontbl.filter: The reconciliation set only, filtered by the reason buttons above and by scope.
recontbl.columns: Why it is not in the count: the state of its first-rehabilitation record. Last status and Last visit: from the activity records when the set was assembled.

rettbl.source: REG.retired on this page: functionality reports marking points retired, copied from a form this build does not pull. No build step recomputes it; it is on the recorded ungenerated backlog.
rettbl.extracted: As copied; the form is not in the build’s extract set.
rettbl.filter: Functionality reports on points in MadAvance’s districts, filtered by scope. They include points outside the managed portfolio, such as abandoned points and rope pumps: this table shows what the report says, not what this page counts.
rettbl.columns: Every column is the report’s own field; nothing is computed.

corrtbl.source: CORR on this page, from data/register_corrections.json, the standing record of corrections to the mWater register, versioned with the report.
corrtbl.extracted: Each entry carries its own evidence date. The nearest-point distances in the evidence are recomputed every run from the register by tools/check_distances.py.
corrtbl.filter: Every correction applied when the page is built; nothing is filtered out.
corrtbl.columns: Evidence that settled it: the dated records the decision rests on, with the nearest other point’s distance computed live.

exctbl.source: CORR on this page, from data/register_corrections.json: the points excluded from the portfolio by a recorded decision.
exctbl.extracted: Each entry carries its own evidence date; distances are recomputed every run by tools/check_distances.py.
exctbl.filter: Every exclusion; an excluded point cannot re-enter the portfolio unless its entry is removed.
exctbl.columns: Evidence: the dated records the exclusion rests on.

efbox.extracted: Each flag carries its own evidence; the file is versioned with the report.
efbox.filter: Points with an eligibility question under methodology 2.2.1(d); these are not data errors.
efbox.columns: Every column is the flag’s own text; nothing is computed.

sdws26tbl.source: SDWS26 on this page, recomputed each run by tools/rebuild_sdws26.py from the annual monitoring survey, form 2eeb8682… (cbn_gender.json), questions WS1.18 (dry season) and WS1.39 (rainy season).
sdws26tbl.filter: Responses that answered both usage questions, by project scenario (deployment). Part-entries that answered neither are excluded, as stated in the section.
sdws26tbl.columns: Served, per season: responses whose answer is every day, more than once a day or every two days, by choice id. Served share: the average of the dry-season and rainy-season shares (James Walker, 23 September 2026). Clusters: communes reached against the VPA-DD B.7.3 minimum. Mean household size: question WS1.12.

popstbl.source: The populations defined in tools/populations.py, exported each run to data/populations.json.
popstbl.extracted: Each population is counted on this run’s extracts; the register was pulled .
popstbl.filter: Every population the page uses, except the build-internal ones.
popstbl.columns: Records: the population’s size this run. The rule, What it reads and The decision: the population’s own declaration, not computed.

chaintbl.source: The reconciliation chain in data/populations.json: each step is a set relation between two populations.
chaintbl.extracted: Counted on this run’s extracts; register pulled .
chaintbl.filter: Every step of the chain from first rehabilitation to the maintained fleet.
chaintbl.columns: Counts: the two population sizes the step relates. Verdict: whether the relation holds.

paramstbl.source: PARAMS on this page: every declared parameter, each with its own citation.
paramstbl.extracted: Not extracted: each parameter was read from its cited document on the date in its Set column.
paramstbl.columns: Value: the declared value. Citation and Set: where it was read and when. Nothing is computed.

marolinta.source: The Marolinta deployment of the borehole-progress form 8764843c… (marolinta_borehole.json), joined to the register’s administrative fields, by tools/marolinta_works.py.
marolinta.filter: Final records on the Marolinta deployment only. Marolinta is outside the carbon programme.
marolinta.columns: Beneficiaries: the field team’s own count on the record. District / commune: from the register where the record lacks them, marked as such.

ttr.source: TTRQ on this page, from data/ttr_table.json, computed each run by tools/render_ttr_table.py from the repair-after-breakdown form 958b4763… (reparation_apres_panne.csv).
ttr.filter: Final repair records that carry both a notification date and a completion date, on any water point: rows by the managed pump’s site, and one row for repairs on points outside the managed register, so the rows add up to the total.
ttr.columns: Median, p90, Mean, Max: days from breakdown notified to repair completed, over the row’s records.

sdws25.source: INSTAT, RGPH-3, Tome 1, Tableau 26: average household size by region and stratum. A published table, not a measurement of ours.
sdws25.extracted: Read from the published table in the evidence folder; it does not change between runs.
sdws25.filter: The regions the programme works in, plus the national figures.
sdws25.columns: Where we work: the live point count in that region.

calcov.source: The gardien-calendar photograph inventory from mWater, machine-read by tools/read_year_ocr.py into data/calendar_extraction_figures.json and data/gardien_calendar_coverage.csv.
calcov.extracted: Reader run of 2026-09-20 over the photographs then on file.
calcov.filter: Points in the managed register on the custody date, one row per site, Marolinta included; the register has gained a point since, so the total can be one short of today’s fleet.
calcov.columns: With a calendar: points with at least one calendar photograph. None ever: points with none. Older than six months: points whose latest calendar photograph is more than six months old. Coverage: with a calendar ÷ points.

calstrata.source: data/calendar_stratum_figures.json, computed by tools/calendar_stratum.py from the calendar reader’s outputs.
calstrata.extracted: Reader outputs of 2026-09-18 to 2026-09-20; stratum computed 2026-09-23.
calstrata.filter: Point-years on the day-call basis with at least the minimum observed window stated above the table. The portfolio row is every such point-year, including the few on points not in the managed register, which have their own row.
calstrata.columns: Mean implied DO and Median: implied days operational per point-year, after subtracting the false-positive floor. Before the floor: the same mean without that subtraction.

caldim.extracted: Stratum computed 2026-09-23 from reader outputs of 2026-09-18 to 2026-09-20.
caldim.filter: Points in the managed register on the custody date, Marolinta included, split by each dimension in turn into those with day calls on the day-call basis and those without. Points, not point-years.
caldim.columns: Evidenced: points with day calls on the day-call basis. Not: the rest. % evidenced: evidenced ÷ (evidenced + not).

calyear.filter: Point-years with a readable sheet whose year could be read, one row per sheet year.
calyear.columns: Median covered: the median share of the point-year carrying photographic evidence, up to the day its latest photograph was taken. At least nine in ten and under half covered: counts of point-years in those bands.

fnrb.source: The fNRB values in PARAMS: registered as in the VPA-DD, SDWS 21 p.76 (MoFuSS; Toliary provincial for Fort-Dauphin), and applied for Maroantsetra at % (James Walker, 21 Sep 2026); PUMPS with the WorldPop allocation for people served.
fnrb.extracted: Register pulled ; allocation run of .
fnrb.filter: Carbon portfolio sites only; Marolinta is outside the carbon programme.
fnrb.columns: fNRB registered: SDWS 21 as registered. fNRB applied: the value the ex post figures use; for Maroantsetra the sub-national %, corrected at verification. People served: the sum of the site’s WorldPop allocations after caps, computed live. The weighted row uses the applied values.

icsdep.source: SDWS26 on this page, recomputed each run by tools/rebuild_sdws26.py from the annual monitoring survey, form 2eeb8682…: questions WS1.31 (dry season) and WS1.52 (rainy season), the household’s main cooking device.
icsdep.extracted: Survey pulled ; counted on every build.
icsdep.filter: All responses on each scenario’s deployment of the survey.
icsdep.columns: Improved: choice J2E4JeG. Three-stone: choice qZ2xJJR. No answer: responses that left the question blank. Proportion: improved ÷ responses that answered.

enduro-disp.source: data/enduro_disposition.csv: Coddy’s managed-sites KML, the earlier Endur’O file, the UNICEF list and the Endur’O mWater group, matched by proximity.
enduro-disp.extracted: Reconciled to the contractor folders on 18 September 2026 (data/enduro_disposition.csv); the Endur’O figures are hand-entered until Endur’O is on mWater.
enduro-disp.filter: Endur’O sites only, one disposition per site.
enduro-disp.columns: Sites: the number of sites given that disposition by the proximity match.

act-close-eight.source: The first-rehabilitation records of the listed pumps on the combined rehabilitation form 86cf66ef…, question 2.2.1(d).
act-close-eight.columns: Every column is the record’s own field; nothing is computed.

cptbl.source: data/carbon_parameters.json: one row per parameter the methodology requires us to evidence, with the population or form that supplies it.
cptbl.extracted: Coverage and the most recent record are computed on every build from the populations and the extract manifest; each extract’s pull date is in data/extract_manifest.json and the register was pulled .
cptbl.filter: Every parameter in the register of requirements; the chips above filter by readiness.
cptbl.columns: Coverage: the share of the relevant set that the supplying population covers. Most recent record: the newest record on the supplying form, and its age. Readiness: derived from coverage and route, as the note below the table states.

erinputs.source: The registered parameters of the VPA-DD and the Gold Standard ERSDWS methodology, each value with its own source in the Source column; fNRB and the days-operational cap from PARAMS; people served from the WorldPop allocation; calendar custody from data/gardien_calendar_coverage.csv via the calendar stratum.
erinputs.extracted: Registered values do not change between runs. People served is live on this page; calendar custody is as at the date in its cell; the register was pulled .
erinputs.filter: One row per input of the baseline-emissions equation above.
erinputs.columns: Value: the registered or applied value, or the live figure it rests on. Evidence status: whether that value is sourced, and whether it is evidenced for the current monitoring period.

fuelsplit.source: Hand pumps: the registered VPA-DD (GS12600_GS12601 VPA-1, VPA-DD V2), SDWS 6 on p.69 and SDWS 8 on p.71, declared as parameters. Moramanga: the piped-water carbon baseline survey Piped Water || Baseline Cbn (3ef4385a619244c7ad129169ac1ec71f), question 4.1.2.2.4.1. Antananarivo: Sustainable Energy for All (2024), “Integrated Energy Access Planning”, as quoted in the VPA-DD, p.72.
fuelsplit.extracted: Survey pulled by the weekly build; the VPA-DD values are fixed at registration.
fuelsplit.filter: Hand pumps: the two carbon districts. Moramanga: every final response on the survey, the four piped systems whose upgrade or new build is under way. Antananarivo: the onboarded kiosk and the sites not yet onboarded alike, until they have a survey of their own.
fuelsplit.columns: Wood, Charcoal, Other fuel: the main fuel for boiling water. For Moramanga it is the dry-season answer, counted per household and divided by all responses (count in brackets). Three-stone fire, Improved cookstove: the share of premises by stove (SDWS 6); not computed for Moramanga.

piped-pairing.source: PIPEDWQ.pairing on this page, from data/piped_wq.json, computed each run by tools/rebuild_piped_wq.py from the piped result form 0ac68d82… (wq_results_piped.json) and the piped sampling form ef8cf735… (wq_sampling_piped.json).
piped-pairing.filter: Final responses on both forms, submitted since the tap-level sampling protocol went live, that are flagged: a result with no unpaired sample at its water point in the hours before it was submitted, a sample with no result after the waiting period, a sample outside the standposts-only protocol, and a pair whose result date disagrees with its sample by more than a day. Other pairs are not listed.
piped-pairing.columns: Water point: the water point code (the system code for a system-level sample). Day: the Madagascar day the sample was taken, or for a result with no sample the time it was submitted. Sample: the sampling record, or for an unpaired result the samples at its water point in the days before it.

imcaptbl.source: PUMPS and the WorldPop allocation (SDWS 1) on this page, and data/india_mark_cap.json, written each build by tools/india_mark_cap.py from the pump installation depth on the retired combined works form 86cf66ef….
imcaptbl.extracted: Works form pulled ; allocation run of .
imcaptbl.filter: The whole managed portfolio, whatever scope is selected: these are the programme’s figures, so they do not move with the scope buttons.
imcaptbl.columns: Current: the figure as the page reports it, every India Mark capped at the applied . Proposed rule: the same figure with each India Mark capped at its proposed value, where its pump is installed at m or less and otherwise. Difference: proposed less current. Every carbon figure on this page uses the current column until James Walker confirms.

sdws18tbl.source: The household water-quality survey, form db0bcbf2… (“Clean Water || project SDWS18”), through data/sdws18.json, written each build by tools/rebuild_sdws18.py.
sdws18tbl.filter: The 2025 round: final records on the deployments SDWS18 (Fort-Dauphin) and SDWS18 (Maroantsetra); drafts left out. Every record is a household (point-of-use) sample. The whole round, whatever scope is selected.
sdws18tbl.columns: The three E. coli columns: samples by E. coli per 100 ml, in the bands shown in their headings. Pass: fewer than per 100 ml, the household rule (Water Quality Protocol v2.1 section 5.1; methodology v2.0 §3.2.3.2), with its exact % confidence interval. No E. coli: the stricter zero count, information only — it is the rule for a pump or tap sample, not for a household one.

sdws18rec.source: Form db0bcbf2… (“Clean Water || project SDWS18 || Survey || Active”), through data/sdws18.json; written each build by tools/render_sdws18.py.
sdws18rec.filter: Every final record on the deployments SDWS18 (Fort-Dauphin) and SDWS18 (Maroantsetra), one row each; drafts excluded. The whole round, whatever scope is selected. The row count equals the tests in the tiles above, and the build fails if it does not.
sdws18rec.columns: Water point and Household: the mWater codes the record is linked to. Result: pass below per 100 ml, the household rule; a row with any E. coli, or a household recorded more than  km from its pump (a probable GPS or linking error, kept in the counts), is marked. mWater record: the response, opened in the mWater portal.

trc1-agreement.source: TRC1 on this page, from data/transcription_round1.json, written by tools/transcription_round1.py from Adriaan Mol’s export of 28 Sep 2026, Dieu Donné Razafimahatratra’s export of 1 Oct 2026 (both in data/transcriptions/) and the machine reading extraction_days2.csv (row-fix run of 30 Sep 2026), joined on the image.
trc1-agreement.extracted: Transcriptions exported on the transcription page, the second at ; read from the files, not from mWater.
trc1-agreement.filter: The calendars both humans confirmed and the machine reads, days inside each sheet’s observed window (sheet year and photo date); calendar 3, the sheets held out and calendar 43’s margin-note days are out. Dieu Donné’s cells after cleaning (round1_ajustements.csv). A day either reader marks ? is shown in the matrices but not scored.
trc1-agreement.columns: Agreement: days both read X or both read blank, over the days both read X or blank. Cohen’s κ: that agreement corrected for chance. Days scored: days neither reads ?. Calendars marked: calendars with at least one X in the window, by both readers, by the first reader of the pair only, by the second only.

trc1-machine.source: TRC1 on this page, from data/transcription_round1.json, written by tools/transcription_round1.py from Adriaan Mol’s export of 28 Sep 2026, Dieu Donné Razafimahatratra’s export of 1 Oct 2026 (both in data/transcriptions/) and the machine reading extraction_days2.csv (row-fix run of 30 Sep 2026), joined on the image.
trc1-machine.extracted: Transcriptions exported on the transcription page, the second at ; read from the files, not from mWater.
trc1-machine.filter: The calendars both humans confirmed and the machine reads, days inside each sheet’s observed window (sheet year and photo date); calendar 3, the sheets held out and calendar 43’s margin-note days are out. Dieu Donné’s cells after cleaning (round1_ajustements.csv). Days the reference reads ? and days the machine reads ? are left out.
trc1-machine.columns: Sensitivity: of the reference’s X, the share the machine also reads X. Specificity: of the reference’s blanks, the share the machine reads blank. X found, X missed: the reference’s X the machine reads X, and reads blank. X the reference reads blank: the machine’s X on a day the reference reads blank. The last row takes as reference only the days the two humans read the same way.

rdiag-causes.source: RVAL on this page, from data/reader_validation.json, written by tools/reader_validation.py from transcription round 1 (data/transcriptions/), the reader of record’s output extraction_days2.csv and the v3 reading of the same photographs. The causes come from data/reader_diagnosis/cells.csv, classed by eye from the crops in that folder.
rdiag-causes.extracted: Crops cut on 1 Oct 2026 from the photographs in the mWater image backup, with the reader’s own geometry (tools/diagnose_reader.py).
rdiag-causes.filter: The days both human readers marked X in round 1, on the calendars both confirmed and the machine reads, inside each sheet’s observed window; one row per cause.
rdiag-causes.columns: Why the reader missed it: the main reason, one per day. X days: how many of the both-X days it explains. What happened: what the crop shows.

rdiag-metrics.source: RVAL on this page, from data/reader_validation.json, written by tools/reader_validation.py from transcription round 1 (data/transcriptions/), the reader of record’s output extraction_days2.csv and the v3 reading of the same photographs.
rdiag-metrics.extracted: Round-1 transcriptions exported 28 Sep and 1 Oct 2026; v2 output of the 30 Sep 2026 run; v3 run on 1 Oct 2026.
rdiag-metrics.filter: Days inside each sheet’s observed window on the round-1 calendars both humans confirmed and the machine reads. All calendars: every one; held-out calendars: the even-numbered ones, which played no part in choosing v3’s threshold. A day the machine reads ? is left out.
rdiag-metrics.columns: Both-X days found: days both humans marked X that the reader also reads X. Sensitivity: that share. Specificity: of the days both read blank, the share the reader reads blank. κ: agreement corrected for chance. The last two columns take each human alone as the reference.

callfollow.source: CALLF on this page, from data/call_followup.json, written by tools/call_followup.py from the call-centre form c08b3fe2…, the preventive-maintenance form de26d89a… and the repair form 958b4763….
callfollow.extracted: Extracts pulled ; as-of date , the activity tiles’ own.
callfollow.filter: Managed pumps a submitted call reported down, or partially working for a reason other than a routine service request, in the last days; one row per pump, from its first such call in the window.
callfollow.columns: Call: the date of that call, linked to the record. Next record: the first submitted repair or preventive visit after the call, with days elapsed. Next repair: the first repair after the call. Repaired in time: a repair within days of the call, none after that, or a call too recent to say.

hyg-months.source: HYG on this page, from data/hygiene.json, written by tools/rebuild_hygiene.py from the hygiene-promotion form 283c5670… and the annual Hygiene&San survey 209cc5fc….
hyg-months.filter: Submitted sessions on water points in the managed register, in the districts the scope covers, by month of the visit date; months with none are shown.

hyg-years.source: HYG on this page, from data/hygiene.json, written by tools/rebuild_hygiene.py from the hygiene-promotion form 283c5670… and the annual Hygiene&San survey 209cc5fc….
hyg-years.filter: Each calendar year, the districts the scope covers. Survey households: submitted Hygiene&San responses at a managed point where the handwashing place could be asked about (community households, permission given).
hyg-years.columns: Sessions, Water points reached: sessions recorded and distinct managed points they were held at. JMP survey households: households asked the JMP core hygiene questions. With basic hygiene: share with a handwashing place observed with water and soap. Meets the obligation: at least one session and a JMP-question survey that year.

hyg-last.source: HYG on this page, from data/hygiene.json, written by tools/rebuild_hygiene.py from the hygiene-promotion form 283c5670… and the annual Hygiene&San survey 209cc5fc….
hyg-last.filter: One row per district in the scope.
hyg-last.columns: Sessions on record: all submitted sessions at managed points in the district. Last session: the latest visit date.

sdws18six.source: SDWS18 on this page, from data/sdws18.json, written by tools/rebuild_sdws18.py from the household water-quality survey db0bcbf2… and the works records: the first-rehabilitation records on the combined works form 86cf66ef… (“Date de début des travaux”) and the borehole-progress form.
sdws18six.filter: Every water point sampled in the 2025 household round, by district. The rule, as ruled by James Walker on 1 Oct 2026: counted per pump from its installation or rehabilitation date, in every annual round.
sdws18six.columns: Installed or rehabilitated: the works date, from a successful first-rehabilitation record where there is one. First household sample: the earliest sample at that pump in the round. Days after the works: between the two. Six-month rule: inside when the sample falls at least six months after the works.

enduro-reg-compare.source: ENDUROREG on this page, from data/enduro_registry.json, written by tools/rebuild_enduro_registry.py from the Endur’O mWater group’s water systems and water points (piped_systems.csv, enduro_points.csv), beside the hand-entered data/enduro_manual.json.
enduro-reg-compare.extracted: Entity extracts pulled . Hand-entered figures as at the dates in the last column.
enduro-reg-compare.filter: Every water system and water point managed by the Endur’O group, whatever its status.
enduro-reg-compare.columns: Hand-entered: the figure in data/enduro_manual.json. Registered in mWater: the live count. Difference: registered minus hand-entered; negative means fewer are registered than the hand-entered figure.

enduro-reg-schemes.source: ENDUROREG on this page, from data/enduro_registry.json, written by tools/rebuild_enduro_registry.py from the Endur’O mWater group’s water systems and water points (piped_systems.csv, enduro_points.csv).
enduro-reg-schemes.filter: One row per registered water system, then the water points whose water system is not set, then the total.
enduro-reg-schemes.columns: Type: the system’s mWater management type. GPS, Photo: whether the system record carries them. Water points: points whose water system is this one, with their mWater types; With GPS, With photo: how many of them carry each.

enduro-smartap.source: ENDUROREG on this page, from data/enduro_registry.json, written by tools/rebuild_enduro_registry.py from the Endur’O mWater group’s water systems and water points (piped_systems.csv, enduro_points.csv).
enduro-smartap.filter: Endur’O water points named SMARTAP and a number.
enduro-smartap.columns: Water system: the parent system the record names. deviceID: the meter id read from the description. GPS, Photo: whether the record carries them.

piped-wq-taps.source: ENDUROREG on this page, from data/enduro_registry.json, written by tools/rebuild_enduro_registry.py from the Endur’O mWater group’s water systems and water points (piped_systems.csv, enduro_points.csv), and the piped sampling form ef8cf735… and result form 0ac68d82….
piped-wq-taps.filter: Registered Endur’O taps with at least one final sample matched to them, by tap code or deviceID, or by position within the matching distance.
piped-wq-taps.columns: Samples, First, Last: the matched samples and their sampling days. Sampling points: the grouped sampling points that landed on the tap. System results: final results on the result form naming the tap’s water system; results do not yet name a tap.

piped-wq-unmatched.filter: Sampling points (final samples grouped by position) with no registered Endur’O water point within the matching distance.
piped-wq-unmatched.columns: Recorded type: the point type entered on the samples. Nearest registered tap, Distance: the closest registered Endur’O water point and how far it is from the sampling point’s centre.

elig-hp.source: ELIG on this page, from data/eligibility.json, written by tools/rebuild_eligibility.py from the first-rehabilitation records on the retired combined works form 86cf66ef… and its successor 63747997….
elig-hp.filter: Every pump in the managed fleet in the selected scope; where a pump has several first-rehabilitation records, the one that best evidences eligibility (Yes with photographs, then Yes, then the latest).
elig-hp.columns: Out of order three months before: the control question ea3e342a…, as answered. Photographs: photographs on a4d23938… proving the pump was not working. Works date: the date the works began, else the record’s submission date. Record: the response in mWater.

elig-gaps.source: ELIG on this page, from data/eligibility.json, written by tools/rebuild_eligibility.py, from the 2.2.1(d) flags in data/register_corrections.json and the records they name.
elig-gaps.filter: The records flagged under methodology 2.2.1(d): the control answered No or left blank, in the managed fleet or not.
elig-gaps.columns: Fleet: whether the pump is in the managed fleet. Photographs, Works date, Record: as in the full table. Action: what closes the gap.

elig-piped.source: ELIG on this page, from data/eligibility.json, written by tools/rebuild_eligibility.py from data/piped_systems_status.json and the piped result form 0ac68d82….
elig-piped.filter: Every water system in Endur’O’s mWater group; final results naming the system, dated before the protocol went live or before the system’s works completion.
elig-piped.columns: Pre-project results, Dates: those results. With E. coli: the share above the pass maximum. Eligibility: non-potable shown when at least one fails. Records: the list of responses, each linked.

chgfig.source: data/change_review.json, written each build by tools/change_review.py: the four headline figures as the page computes them, on last week’s edition and on this one.
chgfig.extracted: Both pages are evaluated in the headless browser at build time; last week’s edition is the last one published before this Monday.
chgfig.filter: The four headline figures, in the default scope (all water points in scope).
chgfig.columns: Last week and This week: the figure on each edition. Days operational is the applied value.

chgcause.source: data/change_review.json, written each build by tools/change_review.py, from each moved point’s mWater records and their history (created, submitted, edited, approved, rejected; who and when).
chgcause.extracted: From the extracts pulled for this build.
chgcause.filter: Water points whose portfolio membership, people served, water test, works date, status or eligibility differs from last week’s edition.
chgcause.columns: Water points: how many moved for each cause.

chgpts.extracted: From the extracts pulled for this build, against last week’s edition.
chgpts.filter: Every water point that moved; a very long week is cut short and its full list kept in data/change_review.json.
chgpts.columns: What changed: last week → this week. Cause: the record behind the change, or a repository edit where no record changed.

chgflags.source: data/approvals.json and each week’s Asana approval task, read by tools/change_review.py.
chgflags.extracted: Approval state read from Asana at each build.
chgflags.filter: Weeks with changes of major impact (a, b or c) not yet approved by Adriaan or Jan.
chgflags.columns: Status: the approval state and who gave it; What waits: each flagged change.

repeatbd.source: data/repeat_breakdowns.json, written each build by tools/repeat_breakdowns.py from the repair records on both repair sources (the retired combined form and the live repair form).
repeatbd.extracted: From the repair extracts pulled for this build.
repeatbd.filter: Managed hand pumps, ranked by repairs in the last twelve months; the twelve with the most.
repeatbd.columns: Repairs, past year (the twelve months to the latest repair on file) and Repairs, all: final or pending repair records naming the pump, by completion date (else notification, else submission date). Last: the latest.
